# Optimized critical normals: the physical Schur form and its coverage cost

This note concerns actual cap masses as BOTH bodies and their through-source normals vary. It proves the local reduced Hessian, states precisely what remains valid for a singular normal Hessian, and calculates an actual three-triangle example. Normal optimization removes a real cap-curvature term. Requiring the selected circuit itself to preserve full-fiber coverage restores exactly that term in the example.

The archived Schur complement in `candidate b4c3b9c6a52059d2` is a different object: support curvature of a constrained moment body. The physical cap calculation here does not identify those two Hessians, assume a global variational minimizer, or prove OC.

## 1. The regular physical normal envelope

Let h be coordinates for an actual finite-dimensional compatible body family, optionally including a specified smooth source point in one fixed integer fiber. Let theta be local coordinates for all through-source nonvertical normals: integer tilt plus continuous angular coordinates, with one continuous coefficient normalized to one. Write Phi(h,theta) for the ORIGINAL mixed cap mass.

Assume Phi is C² near (h0,theta0), theta0 is stationary in all its normal coordinates, and

    A=Phi_hh, B=Phi_h theta, K=Phi_theta theta>0             (1)

at that point. Open proper-cut polygonal chambers supply analytic examples: vertices and cut intersections are rational functions of support and normal parameters with nonzero denominators. Properness alone, without a stable transverse chamber or other C² justification, is not asserted sufficient.

There is a unique nearby stationary normal theta(h), it is a strict local normal minimum, and its optimized cap branch V(h)=Phi(h,theta(h)) satisfies

    DV=Phi_h,
    D²V=A-B K^(-1) B^T.                                  (2)

Proof. Apply the implicit function theorem to Phi_theta=0. Its derivative in theta is the invertible K, giving Dtheta=-K^(-1)B^T. Positive definiteness persists locally and ensures a strict local minimum. Differentiate V once; the normal-gradient term vanishes. Differentiate that identity once more and substitute Dtheta to obtain (2). All these operations concern one actual moving cap through the prescribed actual source.

This is only a local branch until competing normals are controlled. If the original normal is the unique global minimizer on a common compact normal parameter set, a positive gap outside its neighborhood makes V the actual all-normal minimum nearby. With finitely many global minimizers, each satisfying (1), the actual minimum is the minimum of their branches, once the same compact-gap argument is applied. The finite-base finite-tilt compactification in `candidate 867dbbe22c30cda2`, Section 1, gives such a common compact set for bounded nearby bodies and sources in a fixed positive interior fiber.

## 2. Singular normal Hessians and the exact constrained quadratic cost

If K is merely positive semidefinite, fix a physical body velocity v and put b=B^T v. The quadratic coefficient minimized over linear normal velocities w is

    inf_w [v^T A v+2b^T w+w^T K w].                       (3)

It is finite if and only if b belongs to range K. In that case it equals

    v^T A v-b^T K^dagger b,                               (4)

and the minimizing velocities are -K^dagger b+ker K. If b is not in range K, its component in ker K supplies a linear term of either sign and (3) is -infinity. These statements follow by orthogonally diagonalizing K and completing squares in its positive eigenspaces.

Even when the range condition holds, (4) need not be the Hessian of an actual minimized value function. Nonlinear normal responses can occur at larger scales than h. For example Phi(h,theta)=theta^4+h theta² has an isolated normal minimum at (0,0), K=B=A=0, but its minimized value is 0 for h>=0 and -h²/4 for h<0; minimizing normals on the latter side have size sqrt(-h/2). Thus a pseudoinverse formula alone cannot replace an implicit-branch or higher-order argument. This is a general analytic qualification example, not a claimed mixed-body construction.

For positive definite K, additional LINEARIZED normal-incidence constraints have an exact cost. If normal velocities must satisfy Rw=d(v), and that system is feasible, completing squares gives

    min_(Rw=d) [v^T A v+2b^T w+w^T K w]
      =v^T A v-b^T K^(-1)b
       +e^T [R K^(-1)R^T]^dagger e,
    e=d(v)+R K^(-1)b.                                   (5)

The vector e belongs to range R, hence to range(RK^(-1)R^T). To prove (5), set q=K^(1/2)(w+K^(-1)b). Then the remaining minimization is the least squared norm subject to R K^(-1/2)q=e. Orthogonal decomposition into the kernel and row space proves the displayed pseudoinverse formula. It retains redundant incidence equations without assuming full row rank.

## 3. An actual globally critical three-fiber calibration

Put

    T=conv{(-1,-1),(2,-1),(-1,2)}, |T|=9/2,
    C0=[-1,1] times T.

The three actual integer fibers are T at j=-1,0,1; total area is 27/2. The source Y=(0,0,0) is actual and interior to its positive middle fiber. Its raw mixed depth is 6, and its only minimizing normal directions are the three cylindrical canonical caps

    x>=0, y>=0, -x-y>=0.                                 (6)

Here is the complete dependency for this assertion. Every through-source cap has an own-middle area at least Gamma_2|T|=2. Its two endpoint areas, in the same continuous direction with opposite integer thresholds, have sum at least 2 f_T(0)=4 by the proved all-direction identity in `candidate 4ffd81a5b3e6f9fb`. That theorem includes every threshold, empty/full status, and all continuous directions. Thus every nonvertical cap has mass at least 6; vertical caps have mass 9. Each cap in (6) has mass exactly 6.

Equality requires that the middle own cap have area 2. The ordinary triangle proof gives precisely the three canonical centroid directions in (6). In the x direction, with integer tilt alpha, the two endpoint areas are 4+alpha² for |alpha|<=1 and at least 9/2 for |alpha|>=1. Thus their sum equals 4 only at alpha=0. Cyclic vertex permutation proves the same for the other directions. This establishes the complete three-element global normal menu. Finally, (6) covers all continuous fiber spaces, so no point anywhere in S has depth greater than 6.

Allow nearby aligned actual fibers

    K_j=c_j+r_j T, c_j=(p_j,q_j),

and keep the source at Y=0 in the middle fiber. Near the original array this source remains interior. Use the x-cap chart

    x+alpha j+theta y>=0.

In its open one-vertex proper-cut chamber the EXACT cap mass is

    Phi(h,alpha,theta)
      = [1/(2(1-theta))]
          sum_(j=-1)^1 [2r_j+p_j+alpha j+theta(q_j-r_j)]².  (7)

Indeed the retained vertex is c_j+r_j(2,-1). The normal-margin differences to the other two vertices are 3r_j and 3r_j(1-theta). Multiplying their edge-intercept ratios by the triangle area (9/2)r_j² yields (7). All signs remain strict in a neighborhood.

At r_j=1,p_j=q_j=alpha=theta=0, the normal Hessian is

    K=diag(2,3),                                           (8)

so this actual global critical cap is isolated and nondegenerate in BOTH integer tilt and angular coordinates.

For a body velocity (rho_j,P_j,Q_j), define

    A_j=2rho_j+P_j,
    b_alpha=sum_j j A_j,
    b_theta=sum_j(P_j+2Q_j).

Differentiating (7) gives the exact optimized physical Hessian

    sum_j A_j²
       -(sum_j j A_j)²/2
       -(sum_j(P_j+2Q_j))²/3.                            (9)

This formula is applied only to body velocities allowed by actual compatibility; it does not free the three fibers independently when a midpoint inclusion is active.

## 4. An actual affine-radius mode whose optimized cap curvature vanishes

For |a|<1 let the actual family be

    K_j(a)=(1+a j)T, j=-1,0,1.                           (10)

These radii are affine in the integer base, so the convex hull has exactly the displayed fibers and all midpoint compatibility equalities persist. Its total mass is

    M(a)=27/2+9a².                                      (11)

In (7), the cap formula reduces exactly to

    Phi(a,alpha,theta)
      =6+(3/2)theta²/(1-theta)
          +(2a+alpha-a theta)²/(1-theta).                (12)

Thus its local optimized normal is

    theta=0, alpha=-2a,

and the branch mass is exactly 6. Its normal Hessian there is

    [[2,-2a],[-2a,3+2a²]], determinant 6>0.              (13)

The same holds for each of the three cyclic canonical branches. At a=0 their complete global menu and positive Hessians were proved above. The common finite-tilt compact reduction and the positive gap outside small neighborhoods of these three normals therefore imply: for all sufficiently small |a|, these are still the only all-normal minimizing branches, and the actual middle-source depth is exactly 6. This is an existence of a sufficiently small interval by compactness and continuity, not an assertion for every |a|<1; distant full/empty normal branches may eventually win.

The radius velocity rho_j=j is neutral separately on the even and odd integer parity classes, and it is an actual two-sided compatible velocity. Its frozen cap Hessian is 8; the integer-tilt Schur correction is also 8, giving zero in (9). This is a genuine removal of fixed-cap curvature, not a scalar reweighting of the volume objective.

## 5. Exact cost of making these same three caps keep covering every fiber

Let u1=(1,0),u2=(0,1),u3=(-1,-1), with cyclic indices. Parameterize the three normals by

    u_i+theta_i u_(i+1),

and their integer tilts by alpha_i. All cap planes still pass through the actual middle source. Equal-weight continuous balance holds precisely when theta1=theta2=theta3=theta. Indeed the sum of the normals is sum theta_i u_(i+1), whose zero space consists of equal coefficients.

For this minimal full-rank circuit near the original one, its restrictions cover the ENTIRE continuous space over a fixed base j if and only if j sum_i alpha_i>=0. To see this, the sum of the three margins is j sum alpha_i. If this is nonnegative, all three margins cannot be negative. If it is negative, the rank-two margin map has image the affine plane with that prescribed sum, and therefore attains the three equal negative values. Hence there is an uncovered point. Covering both j=-1 and j=1 consequently forces

    sum_i alpha_i=0.                                     (14)

Within the common proper vertex chamber, cyclic invariance of T gives the exact cap masses

    Phi_i=6+(3/2)theta²/(1-theta)
               +(2a+alpha_i-a theta)²/(1-theta).         (15)

Under (14), the average of the last three squared terms is at least a²(2-theta)². Therefore

    max_i Phi_i >= (3/2+a²)(2-theta)²/(1-theta)
                =6+4a²+(3/2+a²)theta²/(1-theta)
                >=6+4a².                               (16)

Equality is attained at theta=0 and alpha_i=0. Thus the exact optimal largest cap mass in this coverage-preserving chamber is

    6+4a²=Gamma_2 M(a).                                 (17)

The unconstrained optimized tilts alpha_i=-2a violate (14) when a!=0. On the endpoint j with a j>0, all three margins at its actual centroid zero equal -2a j<0, so even a positive-area neighborhood of that actual point is missed. This is actual loss of coverage, not merely a failure to cover distant points outside the body.

The second-order version does not require equal weights to remain fixed. Allow smooth positive balancing weights equal to one at a=0. Since all initial integer tilts are zero, differentiating their balanced drift still forces sum_i alpha_i'=0. The integer-tilt normal Hessian for the three branches is 2I; their mixed force along radius velocity A j is (4A,4A,4A). Formula (5) gives the restored second-derivative cost

    (6A)²/(3/2)=24A².                                  (18)

Additional linearized continuous-balance constraints cannot reduce this cost, and zero angular velocities attain it. Thus it is exactly the same constrained quadratic optimum with variable positive weights. Multiplying by the canonical first stress 3/4 gives 18A², precisely the total-volume second derivative. The affine-radius gain disappears in this coverage-preserving constrained Lagrangian.

## 6. Selected-circuit coverage versus all competing source centers

Requiring these three selected middle cuts alone to cover both endpoints is stronger than necessary for a complete mixed-source cap cover. Each endpoint is exposed in the integer projection. A sufficiently large finite integer tilt can isolate it, so its maximum actual raw depth is exactly its own ordinary maximum:

    2(1-a)² at j=-1,    2(1+a)² at j=1.                    (19)

For sufficiently small |a| both are below 6. The three optimized middle cuts cover the entire MIDDLE fiber because their continuous normals balance and their planes meet at its source. Hence they bound every middle point's mixed depth by 6, and Section 4 provides an actual middle point attaining 6. Adding endpoint-isolating cap circuits, whose budgets have strict slack below 6, gives a complete cover of S. Therefore the true GLOBAL raw maximum remains exactly 6 for all sufficiently small |a|, while (11) increases the total mass. This is a genuine local decrease in maximum normalized depth, still far above OC; the failure of the selected three-cap cover at endpoints is repaired by the other source groups.

For an elementary finite calibration of a different globally deepest fiber, set a=1/2. The larger endpoint has exact depth 9/2, and the smaller has depth 1/2. The middle fiber's depth function is invariant under cyclic vertex permutation and has convex superlevel sets, so its maximum occurs at the fixed centroid 0: average any point's three orbit points within its convex depth superlevel set. A canonical through-centroid cap can be given a finite tilt that fully includes the smaller endpoint and excludes the larger. Its mass is

    2+(9/2)(1-a)²=25/8 < 9/2.

Thus the larger endpoint centroid is an actual globally deepest point at a=1/2. This is a direct upper/lower certificate, not a claim to have identified the exact transition parameter or classified all affine-radius chains. General homothetic three-fiber depth bounds already exist in `candidate aae24573a37976a6`; they are not being reproved here.

## 7. What remains open in this mechanism

Normal optimization changes the physical Hessian by a proved nonnegative Schur correction. Actual incidence and coverage constraints impose the additional nonnegative cost (5), which is exact in the tested family. Slack cap groups can sometimes absorb a selected circuit's lost coverage, as Section 6 proves, so imposing full-fiber coverage on each chosen group can itself be unnecessarily restrictive.

No general theorem here decides which group-cover constraints must remain active at a hypothetical below-OC minimizer, bounds their Schur cost by parity, or produces a simultaneous improving motion for every source group. Such a theorem would need to retain the shared original planes, all actual centers, and every active competing budget. Those are the remaining geometric requirements, not consequences of the unconstrained Schur formula.
